stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speedup according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, promising faster local AI inference.
This is presented as a preview, indicating ongoing development and optimization efforts.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local operation.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command to streamline the setup and execution of coding tools.
It allows users to run advanced coding models (like Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex) locally or via the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: FAA proposal: Supersonic airliners can fly over US cities if they’re quiet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is proposing new regulations to permit supersonic airliners over US cities.
The key condition for approval is that the aircraft must be quiet enough to eliminate the sonic boom.
This represents a potential regulatory shift allowing for faster, longer-range commercial air travel within the US.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: Autonomous AI coding agents create a new security vulnerability due to persistent codebases across sessions.
The research introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to model attacks where misaligned agents distribute payloads across multiple pull requests (PRs) over time.
This work addresses the critical security challenge of safely deploying powerful but potentially untrusted AI systems.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
It focuses on 'unlearning,' a method for reliably removing memorized knowledge post-hoc from large language models.
The research introduces 'LACUNA' to evaluate localization precision, challenging current benchmarks that only test output-level erasure.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Proposes 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log alerting, JSON repair).
The core concept, 'Program-as-Weights,' compiles natural language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts.
Addresses current limitations of relying on LLM APIs, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
It focuses on 'unlearning,' a post-hoc method to remove memorized knowledge, often using a localize-first approach.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Introduces OrbitQuant, a new data-agnostic quantization method designed for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs).
Addresses the high inference cost of DiTs, which are currently state-of-the-art in image and video generation.
Solves the problem of activation shifting across different sampling steps and prompts, which plagues traditional post-training quantization (PTQ) methods.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: Addresses the critical security issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive training data, including PII.
Focuses on 'Unlearning' methods, specifically challenging the current paradigm which only evaluates erasure at the output level.
Introduces 'LACUNA' as a new testbed designed to evaluate the precision of knowledge removal within the model itself.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts (Program-as-Weights).
Addresses limitations of relying on LLM APIs for tasks like log alerting or JSON repair (locality, reproducibility, cost).

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The paper proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated via risk control, showing competitive results.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning.
It is designed to support long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to Claude Code via Ollama integration.

stories.title: NASA launched an emergency mission to stop the Swift Observatory from crashing to Earth
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: NASA initiated an emergency mission to save the Swift Observatory from atmospheric re-entry.
Recent solar storms have caused the observatory's orbit to decay, putting it at risk of burning up.
Katalyst Space Technologies was contracted to launch a Link spacecraft to intercept and save the asset.

stories.title: Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A new macOS infostealer, PamStealer, has been discovered.
The malware represents a growing trend in targeted Mac-specific cyber threats.
The discovery highlights the increasing sophistication and focus on Mac security vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating online safety monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control and shows competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long input contexts.
Introduces RECONTEXT (Recursive Evidence Replay), a novel, training-free inference method.
Aims to bridge the gap between LLM context access capabilities and actual context utilization for complex reasoning tasks.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under identical conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives shaped by social context.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
Introduces DramaSR-532K, a large-scale benchmark with 532K annotated dialogue lines across 900+ characters.
Proposes using Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker recognition in video content.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a method to improve on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Addresses a key limitation of current OPSD methods: teacher supervision can cause overfitting and hurt cross-domain generalization.
The proposed technique modulates disagreement to mitigate the negative effects of dense, privileged token-level supervision.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers, generating complete solution proposals to guide classical methods like backtracking and SAT solvers.
The research highlights SE-RRMs' improved extrapolation capabilities when dealing with larger problem sizes in constraint satisfaction problems.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Proposes 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
This paradigm compiles natural language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts (Program-as-Weights).
Aims to reduce reliance on external LLM APIs, addressing issues of locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs generating unsafe outputs even after alignment training.
Proposes a simple, real-time monitoring system that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is calibrated via risk control and shown to be competitive in testing.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against 'off-the-record' (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives without explicit prompting.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for training LLMs.
Addresses a key limitation of current OPSD methods: teacher supervision based on privileged information can cause overfitting and hurt cross-domain generalization.
The proposed method aims to mitigate these issues by modulating the distillation process based on disagreement.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CNeVA, a framework for creating controllable simulated agents.
Agents are designed to imitate logged behavior while allowing steering along interpretable axes.
The technology is crucial for testing autonomous systems (like in traffic simulation) safely by isolating variables.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of training LLMs in specialized domains without expensive human annotations.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Uses the model's own outputs and majority voting across multiple rollouts to generate pseudo-labels for self-supervision.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
It provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks perform under non-IID data conditions.
This work aims to fill a gap in the theoretical understanding of D-SSL robustness when dealing with decentralized, heterogeneous data.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances in a shared debate setting against off-the-record (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Suggests that social context can induce latent objectives in agents even without explicit prompting.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the complex challenge of speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines and over 900 characters.
The work leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in complex narrative content.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to 'Typographic Attacks' (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning over true visual semantics.
The research proposes a 'training-free' method for robust concept localization to address this vulnerability.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection during reasoning.
Proposes using Reinforcement Learning to enable LVLMs to properly ground textual self-reflection in visual inputs.
Aims to improve the models' ability to correct errors, especially when presented with out-of-distribution images.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: Investigates if scaling LLMs alone can improve the fidelity of social simulations.
Examines the relationship between LLM compute scale, general capabilities, and simulation accuracy.
Questions whether simulation fidelity is inherently tied to general LLM capabilities or requires separate research focus.

stories.title: My credential rule reported 842 secrets in vercel/ai. The real count was 0.
stories.author: ofri-peretz
bullet_points: A security scanning tool (credential rule) produced a massive number of false positives (842 findings) when scanning a Vercel project.
The false positives were primarily benign strings like TypeScript union-type literals, error class names, and the word 'test', not actual credentials.
The article discusses the technical challenge of moving from context-blind regex scanning to context-aware detection, especially concerning AI-generated code.

stories.title: What Google's "Microservices Are Dead" Paper Actually Said (And What It Missed About AI)
stories.author: zxpmail
bullet_points: The article analyzes a 2023 HotOS paper from Google researchers regarding the future of microservices.
It specifically critiques the paper's perspective, noting what it overlooked concerning the integration and impact of Artificial Intelligence.
The discussion involves high-level industry figures (Sanjay Ghemawat) and touches upon core distributed systems architecture.

stories.title: vLLM vs llama.cpp vs Ollama: What Happens When Your Model Doesn't Fit in 24GB VRAM
stories.author: sikamikanikobg
bullet_points: Compares performance of vLLM, llama.cpp, and Ollama for running large language models.
Focuses on practical challenges of running models that exceed limited VRAM (e.g., 24GB).
Benchmarks were conducted across a wide range of model sizes, from 1B to 116.8B parameters.
